====================================================================================================

Russia Is Hunting Civilians in Kramatorsk
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-12
07:49:00 UTC
16:49:00 KST

Kramatorsk is not falling in a single assault. It is being strangled. Russian forces are using first person view (FPV) drones to hunt people in streets and courtyards, dropping guided glide bombs on apartment blocks, and striking vehicles that carry the markings of humanitarian work.
This is not collateral damage. It is a method.
JOIN US ON TELEGRAM
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official.
You do not “accidentally” fly a first-person drone into a vehicle painted with humanitarian markings. You do not accidentally hit a civilian standing in a courtyard when the pilot is purposefully watching and maneuvering a drone towards an innocent victim.
Kramatorsk, like Kherson, is being hunted by drone safaris. Brave humanitarians will still go in and evacuate the elderly, deliver heat and pull the injured out of the rubble, all the while being hunted by soulless drone operators. These are a war crime in plain sight. Document it. Name it. Stop pretending this is just the fog of war.
Drones that see the victim before they kill
FPV drones, including fiber-optic models largely immune to jamming, now operate inside Kramatorsk itself, well behind the line that used to define the “front.” Operators fly them in real time; they see an elderly woman; they choose to kill.
Publicly reported incidents this year include:
• June 6, 2026 – a civilian man killed in a residential area. Ukrainian authorities stated the operator could see the target before impact.
• Sept. 4, 2026 – two civilian cars struck by FPV drones in the city; fires started beside homes.
EU Clears €3.2B Patriot Purchase for Ukraine Under €90B Loan
• Repeated strikes on parked cars, public transport and anyone moving in the open. “Waiter Drones” are left on rooftops overnight and used at first light to attack the unsuspecting.
Ukraine has documented more than 11,000 Russian FPV attacks on civilians nationwide, including double-tap strikes that hit the same site after medics and firefighters arrive.
The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine has already classified the systematic FPV targeting of civilians in Kherson Oblast – known predatorily as “Drone Safaris” – as crimes against humanity. The same pattern is now being recorded across the Donetsk region, including Kramatorsk.
Aftermath of evacuation vehicle destroyed by a drone near Kramatorsk. (Video courtesy Kiwi K.A.R.E)
Glide bombs on homes
Guided aerial bombs – FAB-250s fitted with UMPK kits – are cheap, hard to stop, and used against housing as well as military positions.
• Sept. 9, 2026 – five glide bombs were dropped on Kramatorsk, wounding four civilians (women aged 59, 70 and 74; a man aged 72), damaging 27 private homes and a car.
• Late August – some nine glide bombs hit apartment blocks in Kramatorsk with dozens wounded, including an infant.
• Bridges and crossings have been struck as a warning that the way out can be impeded and ultimately closed.
These strikes sit inside a wider campaign of Shahed-type drones and missiles against Ukraine. Kramatorsk’s daily reality, however, is closer and more personal: an FPV drone patrolling a courtyard; a glide bomb hitting a block of flats; roads that are no longer safe to drive.
Targeting people who come to help
The most damning evidence is the targeting of marked civilian and humanitarian vehicles whose purpose is visible from the air.
To date, the “Road-of-Life” program, which falls under the umbrella of Kiwi K.A.R.E (Kiwi Aid & Refugee Evacuation) charitable trust, has come under enemy fire 11 times with five vehicles completely destroyed: two ambulances, one armored ambulance, and two passenger vehicles. Fortunately, there have been no fatalities however several volunteers have been injured with one person remaining in hospital.
• June 1, 2026 – FPV strike on a clearly marked Civil Protection Department vehicle of the Kramatorsk City Council injuring one official. The city’s military administration called it deliberate as the markings were clearly visible; civilian cars stood nearby.
• Sept. 5, 2026 – a volunteer “Road-of-Life” vehicle was destroyed by a drone attack in Kramatorsk while being loaded for evacuation and aid work.
• Sept. 7-8 – three more “Road-of-Life” vehicles were attacked and destroyed, including an armored ambulance, seriously injuring an evacuation team member who was hospitalized.
• Numerous other missions in the Donetsk-Kharkiv belt has logged well over 100 attacks on staff, vehicles, offices and warehouses.
It is for this reason that humanitarian operations in and around Kramatorsk have become extraordinarily hard: driving under drone nets, detectors are a must in vehicles, teams aborting pickups when a drone threat represents clear and present danger.
Evacuations do still happen albeit with reduced frequency, at a slower pace, and with the recognition of significantly heightened danger. Every kilometer is a calculation.
International humanitarian law requires parties to distinguish civilians from combatants and to spare those who bring aid and conduct evacuations. Russia is doing the opposite – they use attacks on humanitarians as a method of warfare.
A city being emptied on purpose
Kramatorsk still stands. Ukrainian forces still hold it and will for the foreseeable future. But life is leaving. Cafés that were full a year ago are quiet. Supermarket shelves are empty. People stay indoors except for essential movement.
Police and local authorities have said it is time for remaining civilians to leave. Tens of thousands have already been displaced from the Kramatorsk district this year. The method is familiar: isolate the city with drones and bombs, punish movement, hit the rescuers, and wait for the population to drain away.
                                                                                                                                                                         
This is a war crime pattern – not an accident
Kiwi K.A.R.E calls these acts what they are:
• Willful killing and targeting of civilians.
• Attacks on civilian objects and housing.
• Attacks on humanitarian and civil-protection personnel and vehicles displaying distinctive signs.
• Terror against a civilian population to force displacement.
These are prohibited under the Geneva Conventions and customary international humanitarian law. They are being documented, daily, by Ukrainian prosecutors, city authorities, emergency services and independent journalists. The operators who fly a drone into a marked aid vehicle, and those who order the method, must be named and held to account.
What we ask
• Governments and media: treat FPV hunting of civilians and strikes on marked humanitarian vehicles as the war crimes they are – not as “battlefield friction.”
• Donors and partners: frontline aid in Sumy, Donetsk and Kherson is still possible, but only with the equipment, protection and funding levels that match the threat. Well-marked humanitarian vehicles are being destroyed. Replacing them is now a matter of life and death.
• New Zealand and allied governments: sustain political, military and humanitarian support for Ukraine. Isolation of cities like Kramatorsk is a strategy. Silence assists it.

Russia says Ukraine attacked trucks supplying fuel to Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
An official said the strike killed two Russian servicemen and endangered the nuclear power plant
The head of Russia’s state nuclear energy corporation accused Ukraine on Sunday of attacking diesel fuel trucks, killing two Russian servicemen and deliberately jeopardising safety at the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine.
Alexei Likhachev said the attack took place on Friday and also resulted in injuries to other Russian soldiers.
The Zaporizhzhia plant, Europe’s largest with six reactors, was seized by Russian forces in the early weeks of the Ukraine war that broke out in February 2022. Each side has regularly accused the other of actions that endanger safety at the plant and increase the risk of a nuclear accident.
Likhachev issued a statement saying Ukrainian forces had launched “a series of combined strikes” on Friday on fuel trucks which deliver diesel to the station.
“The strikes hit very close to the perimeter of the station’s site,” he said.
“Two servicemen were killed and a large number of Russian soldiers were injured, some seriously. They were all involved in supporting this purely civilian mission.”

Pezeshkian warns against unilateral sanctions at BRICS summit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:38:38 UTC
16:38:38 KST

Speaking at the 18th BRICS Plus summit, Pezeshkian said no country can solve today's global challenges alone. "BRICS must turn the scattered capacities of Global South countries into shared capacity. Iran's geopolitical position and its energy and transit capacities can play an effective role in developing trade and energy routes among members," he said.
 
 
 He said resilience means having the capacity to maintain the path of development and independent decision-making even under pressure. Excessive dependence on limited financial and trade systems makes economies vulnerable to political shocks. "Today, unilateral sanctions are not merely an economic issue; they directly affect food security and people's welfare. Therefore, BRICS must build shared capacity for members' economic resilience by developing trade in national currencies and strengthening the New Development Bank."
 
 
 Pezeshkian said economic resilience without security will not be sustainable. Developments in the region, especially the U.S. and Israeli military aggression against Iran, showed that the effects of targeting a country's economic, energy and development infrastructure quickly transcend its borders and bring regional and global consequences.
 
 
 "The Iranian people have paid a heavy price for these aggressions. Men and women, children and civilians have lost their lives, and infrastructure built over decades for the country's development has been damaged. These events remind us of the heavy responsibility of the international community to protect civilians and prevent the normalisation of attacks on civilian targets," he said.
 
 
 He said the people of Gaza and Lebanon continue to face the consequences of crimes and genocide. "One cannot speak of international law if there is no effective international response to military aggression, the killing of people and the destruction of their lives. Therefore, BRICS must play a more effective role in defending national sovereignty, territorial integrity and the prohibition of the use of force."
 
 
 Pezeshkian identified cooperation as the second pillar. No country alone can solve today's global challenges, he said, and BRICS must turn scattered capacities into shared capability. Sustainability was the third pillar. "Development that increases inequality or places today's costs on future generations will not be sustainable. We must not forget that war is one of the serious causes of environmental destruction. Iran's recent experience showed that damage to energy and industrial infrastructure has consequences beyond economic loss and affects the region's natural resources."
 
 
 He said knowledge and innovation are also determining factors. "BRICS must ensure that artificial intelligence and new technologies do not become tools of domination but means of empowering nations."
 
 
 Pezeshkian said BRICS is no longer merely a framework for cooperation among emerging economies but a sign of growing demand for a more balanced and inclusive world in which no power centre has the right to determine the fate of others. Iran, he said, is ready to put its capacities at the service of BRICS cooperation.
 
 
 "Resilience without cooperation will not last, cooperation without justice is not sustainable, and sustainability without peace and security is not possible. Let us turn BRICS into a platform for converting these principles into practical action," he said.
 
 
 MNA
TEHRAN, Sep. 13 (MNA) – President Masoud Pezeshkian told the BRICS Plus summit that unilateral sanctions are not merely an economic issue but directly affect food security and people's welfare.

Yemeni government forces strike Houthi positions, down 5 drones
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:49:42 UTC
16:49:42 KST

Mohammed Sameai and Sahin Demir
13 September 2026•Update: 13 September 2026
Yemeni government forces said Sunday they carried out airstrikes against Houthi positions, personnel, and military equipment and shot down five drones belonging to the group amid escalating fighting across the country.
The Yemeni Armed Forces’ media center said army aircraft conducted three strikes on Houthi positions and barracks in Al-Taba Al-Sawda and Jabal Al-Munim on the Al-Dhabab front in southwestern Taiz province.
The army-affiliated September Net website separately reported that air forces targeted Houthi personnel, equipment, and vehicles in the coastal city of Dhubab and on northern fronts.
The strikes destroyed vehicles and weapons and killed Houthi fighters, the report said, without providing casualty figures.
In a separate development, the government-aligned Nation’s Shield Forces said its 6th Brigade shot down five Houthi drones in the Al-Aghbara area on the Al-Wazi’iyah front west of Taiz during clashes.
The developments come amid major changes in territorial control in recent days as fighting between government forces and the Houthis, which intensified in early July, continues.
The Houthis have announced taking control of several districts in the western coastal provinces of Al-Hudaydah and Taiz, as well as islands in the Red Sea, including Mayyun Island in the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait.
Government forces, meanwhile, have reported advances in the northern Al-Jawf province near the Saudi border and said they were approaching the provincial capital Al-Hazm.
Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa and several provinces in September 2014. A Saudi-led coalition intervened in March 2015 in support of Yemen’s internationally recognized government.

'Is it okay?' PM Modi pauses speech as Xi appears uncomfortable; Chinese president skips gala dinner
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:45:36 UTC
16:45:36 KST

Xi was visiting India for the first time in seven years.
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi briefly interrupted his opening remarks at the Brics Summit on Saturday after Chinese President Xi Jinping appeared to be uncomfortable.PM Modi turned towards Xi and asked the translator accompanying the Chinese president, “Is it okay?” He repeated the question moments later.It was not immediately clear what had caused Xi’s apparent discomfort. It may have been related to the microphone or the translation of PM Modi’s remarks. There was no immediate official reaction from China.The footage of the speech, shared by Doordarshan, shows the incident between the 4:30- and 5-minute marks. Xi, who was visiting India for the first time in seven years, later attended the Brics Summit and held bilateral talks with PM Modi.
During their 40-minute meeting on the sidelines of the Brics Summit, the two leaders agreed that India and China should take a strategic and long-term view of their relationship and ensure that differences do not turn into disputes.Xi said the current momentum in bilateral ties, built on the resumption of institutional exchanges, an expanding cooperation agenda and growing trade, had been hard-won and should be cherished.
PM Modi welcomed the “steady progress” in relations but underlined that peace and tranquillity in border areas would remain an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral ties.The meeting was the leaders’ third bilateral interaction in two years, following their meetings in Kazan in 2024 and Tianjin last year. It was also their first meeting on Indian soil in seven years.Xi reiterated that India and China were partners, not rivals. However, the Indian readout did not include that formulation.
Border, trade issues on agenda
PM Modi stressed the need for both sides to honour existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.The Indian side said the leaders reaffirmed their commitment to finding a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution to the boundary question, keeping in mind the broader political perspective of bilateral ties and the long-term interests of both countries.Modi also raised India’s trade deficit with China and called for greater predictability in supply chains and meaningful, predictable market access.The two sides discussed the need to address concerns related to structural trade imbalances, supply chains and economic cooperation.Since the 2024 Kazan meeting, which marked the end of the eastern Ladakh border standoff, three rounds of talks between the Special Representatives of India and China have taken place. At their latest meeting, the two sides agreed to work towards an early and substantial outcome on boundary delimitation and border management.
Three ‘mutuals’ guide ties
The leaders also noted progress in people-to-people relations and stressed the need to promote cultural exchanges, business ties and greater mobility.“Prime Minister highlighted that both sides must be guided by three mutuals- mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest,” the Indian readout said.They also agreed to expand common ground on regional and global issues and cooperate in addressing shared challenges.Xi called for a more rational and forward-looking strategic assessment of bilateral relations, win-win cooperation, mutual respect and understanding, and inclusive multilateral cooperation.
Xi skips gala dinner
Xi Jinping, however, did not attend a gala dinner hosted by PM Modi for Brics leaders, partner countries and representatives of international organisations, sources aware of the matter told PTI.The reason for his absence was not immediately known. A source suggested that Xi had returned to his hotel to rest after a busy day.Abu Dhabi Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed, who left for home after attending the summit, was also absent from the dinner.Russian President Vladimir Putin and other Brics leaders attended the event. Union ministers, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla and several chief ministers were also present.Union ministers at the dinner included Amit Shah, Nirmala Sitharaman, Piyush Goyal, Ashwini Vaishnaw and Shivraj Singh Chouhan. Chief ministers Yogi Adityanath, Devendra Fadnavis, Suvendu Adhikari and Himanta Biswa Sarma also attended.
The ministers and chief ministers travelled in two buses from Parliament House to Bharat Mandapam, where the dinner was held.The dinner menu featured khandvi mille-feuille, khumb galouti, paneer lababdar, gucchi marmik, carrot-bean poriyal and millet pulao.The dessert menu included Old Delhi fruit cream with jalebi and shahtoot phirni. India is hosting the Brics Summit on September 12-13, with leaders from the 11 member countries and 10 partner countries, along with representatives of international organisations, attending the event.

Her reporting also focuses on policy, governance and economic developments, with a close lens on how decisions in corridors of power affect everyday lives and community well-being.

Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi meet Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim over breakfast
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-13
07:38:29 UTC
16:38:29 KST

The meeting came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks with Ibrahim on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit
NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Sunday met Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim over breakfast on the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra was also present at the meeting. Pictures shared by the Congress showed Rahul Gandhi and Anwar Ibrahim engaged in conversation over breakfast, with the two also seen shaking hands and exchanging smiles.Ibrahim later described Rahul Gandhi as his "good friend" in a post on X, saying the meeting provided an opportunity to exchange views on developments around the world and in the region."Had the opportunity once again to meet my good friend, who is also the Leader of the Opposition in the Indian Parliament, Rahul Gandhi, this morning over breakfast. This brief meeting provided space for us to exchange views on the latest international and regional developments," the Malaysian prime minister said.
The meeting came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi held talks with Ibrahim on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit. Their discussions focused on strengthening cooperation in areas including trade, semiconductors, infrastructure and defence.
Malaysia is a partner country in the BRICS grouping and is also an important partner for India within the ASEAN framework.The breakfast meeting took place as the BRICS Summit entered its final day, with leaders gathering at Bharat Mandapam for an open session on ‘Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability: Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth’.
The summit has focused heavily on global geopolitical and economic challenges. The New Delhi Declaration 2026, adopted on Saturday, expressed deep concern over the escalation of tensions in West Asia and called for maximum restraint.Addressing the summit on Sunday, PM Modi said rising geopolitical tensions were adversely affecting ordinary people across the world and called for greater BRICS cooperation to tackle challenges facing the Global South.He also raised concerns over the "weaponisation of technology and critical minerals", saying such developments could hinder shared progress and prosperity.
